# On android a window's `@key` is a hardware keyboard's key that nothing
# focused took: the activity's window callback hears what Compose passed up
# from the focused composable, and a test presses one into the decor view as
# the system would. A key pressed with nothing focused reaches the window,
# named as a browser names it, and one typed into a focused field is the
# field's. Before, a test's `c.main.key(…)` lowered to no action at all.

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin keys.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

-- keys.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

component app root {
    var heard = ""
    var text = ""
    var pressed = 0

    ui.window #main(title="Keys", @key(k) { heard = heard + "[" + k + "]" }) {
        ui.vbox {
            ui.button #go(text="go", focusable=false, @click { pressed += 1 })
            ui.input #field(:value=text)
            ui.text(value=heard)
        }
    }
}

app()

func testKeysNothingTakesReachTheWindow(t test.Test, c app) {
    for var k = ["7", "+", "A", " ", "Backspace", "ArrowLeft", "Enter", "Escape"] {
        c.main.key(k)
    }
    t.assert(c.heard == "[7][+][A][ ][Backspace][ArrowLeft][Enter][Escape]")
    t.assert(c.pressed == 0)
}

func testAFocusedFieldTakesWhatIsTyped(t test.Test, c app) {
    c.field.focus()
    c.main.key("h")
    c.main.key("i")
    t.assert(c.text == "hi")
    t.assert(c.heard == "")
}
